Labs

Tests, in public.

Labs is where NASHA will publish real tests and what we learn from them. It is empty today because nothing has been tested.

No entries yet. Labs publishes only real tests, with results, including failures. When there is a first test, it will appear here.

How Labs works

  • Only real events are published as events.
  • Failures are published too.
  • Every entry says what was tested, what happened, and what we change next.
  • Nothing is staged and nothing is backdated.
  • Recipes and supplier terms stay private; lessons do not.

The path from here

  1. Now

    Concept and design

    We are specifying the food, beer, place and brand, and preparing real tests.

    Needs: Nothing to prove yet. This stage is about being precise.

  2. Next

    Testing, tastings and pop-ups

    Cooking the first dishes, talking to future guests, and running small events.

    Needs: Permits understood, a kitchen, a partner brewery where beer is involved, and thresholds set before we start.

  3. Then

    A small mobile kitchen or a brewery residency, if validated

    A way to serve people regularly and learn from real orders.

    Needs: Evidence that people come back, and a clear legal path for any beer.

  4. Future

    NASHA brewery and kitchen

    A permanent place with visible brewing, a full kitchen and a shaded court.

    Needs: A site, professionals, capital, and everything above working.

NASHA is a future Indo-Mex brewery and kitchen in Austin, Texas, in development.

The name was chosen by the founder. Legal clearance of the name is pending. Nothing here claims trademark ownership. There is no brewery, restaurant or truck open, and nothing is for sale.

In Hindi and Urdu, nasha means intoxication or addiction. We chose it for the feeling of being captivated by food and beer. We take that meaning seriously and will never present excess or addiction as something to admire. Cultural advisors will review the name and our language before launch.

Menu items are designs for testing, not served food. Heat levels and vegetarian labels describe how a dish is designed, not a certified allergen or dietary statement. Ask before you eat if you have an allergy. If you drink, drink responsibly. Alcohol is for adults of legal drinking age.

Illustrations on this site are original vector drawings made for this project. See how we track asset rights. Build of 2026-10-11.
